page: Microsoft Azure F1als_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by a dedicated single-core AMD EPYC 9V45 processor on the x86_64 architecture, operating at clock frequencies up to 4.5 GHz. The instance is configured with 1 vCPU (1 physical core and 1 thread), supported by 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory is sized at 2.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage, relying instead on network-attached storage options, and contains zero GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong per-core computational capabilities alongside overall throughput limits resulting from the single-vCPU ceiling. The instance scores in the top 10% for single-core stress-ng performance (3699.88) and single-threaded compression benchmarks, delivering 40.65 GB/s in gzip compression and 17.87 GB/s in bzip3 decompression. These figures reflect the high clock speed and modern vector instructions including AVX-512 and VAES. Conversely, aggregate multi-core metrics, database operations (1467.33 on PassMark), and Redis SET operations (3.7 million ops/sec) place in the lower quartiles relative to larger multi-core instances. Memory write bandwidth to large blocks reaches 32.14 GB/s, while cached read bandwidth and overall PassMark memory scores remain low.

From an infrastructure efficiency standpoint, the F1als_v7 provides low-overhead access to modern enterprise AMD EPYC processing power without the expense of unneeded parallel cores. The primary operational tradeoff is the compact 2.0 GB memory footprint and lack of native local storage, which eliminates memory-heavy applications and local caching. Consequently, Microsoft Azure F1als_v7 is best fitted for lightweight batch processing, single-threaded automation scripts, background utility workers, microservice hosting, and basic CI/CD test runners.
